title: Application Insights Requests, Dependencies, and Failures
description: Use the Application Insights performance and failures blades to diagnose slow requests and dependency issues.

data.text: Application Insights automatically tracks incoming HTTP requests. Each request is recorded with its URL, response code, duration, and correlation ID. You can view request patterns, identify slow endpoints, and detect anomalies.

Dependencies are outgoing calls your application makes, such as REST API calls, SQL queries, and storage operations. Application Insights tracks each dependency call with its type, target, duration, and success status, helping you identify external bottlenecks.

data.title: Track a Dependency Manually (C#)
data.content: When auto-collection is not available, track dependencies manually:

rows: Outgoing HTTP, SQL, Redis, blob calls

data.text: The Failures blade in Application Insights groups exceptions by type and shows the most common failure reasons. You can drill into a specific failure to see the full stack trace, affected users, and the requests that led to the error.

data.title: Correlation IDs Link Everything
data.text: Application Insights automatically assigns an operation ID to each request. All dependencies and traces generated during that request share the same ID, allowing you to trace the full call chain.

data.title: View End-to-End Details in the Portal
data.text: In Application Insights, navigate to: Transactions -> Failed requests -> Select an operation -> View end-to-end details.

data.title: Diagnose a Slow Dependency
data.description: Use Application Insights to find why an API endpoint is slow.
steps: Open the Performance blade in Application Insights.
Click through to see the dependency breakdown.
Identify which external dependency is causing the delay.
